regions.summary: Li River plain, west of Dongting Lake: Li county (85% of people), a bit of Linli and Jinshi.

candidates.name: Lizhou
candidates.meaning: Prefecture named for the Li River (Li Shui), mentioned in the Yu Gong; the prefecture lay north of the river.
candidates.fit: Seat was Liyang, today's Li county town, which is most of this region; the prefecture also held Anxiang, Shimen and Linli, so it suits the whole Li basin.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 315 hits with 湖南, top ones about this place (Lizhou Road, Lizhou city wall, Lizhou diocese).
candidates.source_note: 古为澧州，因澧水贯穿全境而得名; CHGIS 澧州 590-1911 seat at 澧阳镇

candidates.name: Lixian
candidates.meaning: County named for the Li River.
candidates.fit: Holds 87% of the county and the county is 85% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 澧县位于洞庭湖西岸，澧水中下游

regions.notes: Lizhou and Lixian are the same place; pick one. Region 4 next door is the other half of the Li basin, so avoid giving it a Li name.

regions.summary: Linxiang, Yunxi and the Hubei counties Jiayu and Chibi across the Yangtze.
Eastern Dongting Lake and Yangtze south bank: Huarong, Shishou (Hubei) and Junshan.

candidates.name: Huarong
candidates.meaning: "Splendid Rong": from Rong city, an old Chu town; the Huarong road is where Guan Yu let Cao Cao go in Romance of the Three Kingdoms.
candidates.fit: Holds 82% of the county, which is 44% of the region's people.
candidates.recognisability: Current county, famous through the Huarong Dao episode.
candidates.source_note: 以“华丽的容城”得名; 古华容道

candidates.name: Junshan
candidates.meaning: Island in Dongting Lake (old names Xiangshan, Dongting Shan), burial place of the two Xiang consorts; home of Junshan Yinzhen tea.
candidates.fit: Junshan district is 20% of the region and the island itself lies in this part of the lake.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 478 hits with 湖南, top ones about the island and the tea.
candidates.source_note: 君山位于湖南岳阳西部的洞庭湖中，是一个小岛

candidates.name: Shishou
candidates.meaning: "Stone head": a lone rock on the Yangtze bank at the city.
candidates.fit: Holds 67% of the city, which is 27% of the region; Hubei, so a second province in the name.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.
candidates.source_note: 因“有石孤立”于城区江边、以石为首而得名

regions.notes: Region sits across the Hunan/Hubei border.

regions.summary: Anxiang, Shimen, Jinshi and most of Linli, between Li River and the lake.

candidates.name: Anxiang
candidates.meaning: "Peaceful countryside": the county name dates from 589, the Sui.
candidates.fit: Holds 98% of the county, which is 36% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 安乡县 589-1911, seat at Anxiang

candidates.name: Jinshi
candidates.meaning: "Ferry market": a river port at the meeting of the Li and its branches.
candidates.fit: Holds 86% of the city, which is only 13% of the region and the smallest of the four units.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.
candidates.source_note: Jinshi appears in the facts as a unit; no separate article in sources.md

candidates.name: Shimen
candidates.meaning: "Stone gate": named for rock walls standing like a gate by the county town.
candidates.fit: Holds only 41% of the county but the county is 18% of the region; its seat was an early commandery seat (Tianmen, Shimen).
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 县名...俱说明系地形特征而得名

regions.notes: Linli (20% of people, 75% of the county) is not listed: the name only reads as a county that borders Li.

regions.summary: Yueyanglou district (80%) and part of Yueyang county.
regions.notes: The label 'yue yang' is drawn on the teal patch here, partly over region 2's boundary.

regions.summary: Dongting Lake polders: Nan county (49%) and Yuanjiang (35%), plus bits of Huarong.

candidates.name: Nanxian
candidates.meaning: Short for Nanzhou, the "south island" of silt that rose from the lake after the Ouchi breach of 1852.
candidates.fit: Holds 96% of the county, which is 49% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county, though a young one (1890s).
candidates.source_note: 土人名之曰‘南洲’; 南洲直隶厅 1895

candidates.name: Dongting
candidates.meaning: Name of China's second-largest freshwater lake (Dongting Lake, the "cave court" of the Xiang consorts' legends), taking in the Xiang, Zi, Yuan and Li rivers.
candidates.fit: Region 6 is the silted lake plain between the Jingjiang outflows and the Zi and Yuan mouths (South Dongting and the polders), the heart of the lake country; East Dongting lies in regions 3 and 5 (Yueyang), West Dongting in region 9. Used alone it would read as claiming the whole lake, which regions 3, 5, 9 and 12 also touch, so 洞庭湖区 (Dongting lake district) or South Dongting would be more exact.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article (洞庭湖), 658 hits with 湖南, top ones about the lake.
candidates.source_note: 岳阳市: 东洞庭湖...汇湘资沅澧四水; 湘阴县: 南洞庭湖滨、湘资两水尾闾

candidates.name: Yuanjiang
candidates.meaning: Named for the Yuan River, which reaches Dongting Lake here.
candidates.fit: Holds 68% of the city, 35% of the region; the old county seat and urban core lie in region 14, not here.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.
candidates.source_note: 地处沅水得名

candidates.name: Nanzhou
candidates.meaning: "South island": the name locals gave the new silt land; Nanzhou Hall (1894-1911) was seated at Wuzui.
candidates.fit: Covers the Nan county area, the core of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article but only 80 hits with 湖南, mostly a town name and a Zhuzhou township.
candidates.source_note: 南洲直隶厅 (1894-1911) seat 乌嘴, CHGIS

regions.notes: Yuanjiang is also offered in region 14; choose it in only one.
Miluo city proper (Miluo Chengguanzhen) falls in region 13, not here, so region 13 cannot reuse the name.

regions.summary: Changde city: Wuling district (78%) and the Dingcheng side.

candidates.name: Changde
candidates.meaning: "Constant virtue" (Changde fu, from 1165).
candidates.fit: Holds the old centre of the prefecture city (5.3M prefecture); regions 8 and 9 are its urban area.
candidates.recognisability: Current prefecture city.
candidates.source_note: 常德府 1165-1911 seat in Changde urban area

candidates.name: Wuling
candidates.meaning: Han commandery (47 onward) seated here, and the old name of Changde; also the Wuling of the Peach Blossom Spring tale.
candidates.fit: Seat in the urban core; Wuling district is 78% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; shares its name with the Wuling mountains, which a west Hunan batch may use.
candidates.source_note: 常德市，古称武陵; CHGIS 武陵郡 47-757

regions.notes: Wuling is also a mountain range name; check with the west Hunan batch before using it.

regions.summary: Hanshou county (62%) and the Dingcheng district lakeside, on west Dongting Lake.

candidates.name: Longyang
candidates.meaning: County name from 222 to 1911 (Longyang county, renamed Hanshou in 1912); the later "Dragon Yang" prefecture and army were seated here too.
candidates.fit: Seat is today's Hanshou town, the largest part of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 102 hits with 湖南, top ones about Hanshou's own street and the Langzhou prefecture.
candidates.source_note: 下辖武陵县、龙阳县（今湖南省汉寿县）; CHGIS 龙阳县 222-1911

candidates.name: Hanshou
candidates.meaning: Han Shou, a Han county (134 onward) whose original seat was in Dingcheng district.
candidates.fit: Holds 91% of the county, which is 62% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county, home of Guan Yu's title Marquis of Hanshou.
candidates.source_note: CHGIS 汉寿县 134-588 at 鼎城区断港头乡城址村

regions.summary: Taoyuan county (74%) on the lower Yuan River, plus a piece of Yuanling.

candidates.name: Taoyuan
candidates.meaning: "Peach spring": named for Taohuayuan, the Peach Blossom Spring of Tao Yuanming's tale.
candidates.fit: Holds 95% of the county, which is 74% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county, very well known through the fable.
candidates.source_note: 因境内有桃花源而得名

candidates.name: Yuanling
candidates.meaning: County on the middle Yuan River.
candidates.fit: Only 37% of the county and 20% of the region; the rest of Yuanling belongs to the west Hunan batch.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.

regions.notes: Taoyuan is spelled like the Taiwan city and airport but the characters differ (桃源 vs 桃園).

regions.summary: Pingjiang county (87%) and a bit of Xiushui.
Yiyang city: Heshan (41%) and Ziyang districts, plus Xiangyin county north of the Xiang.

candidates.name: Yiyang
candidates.meaning: "Yang (north bank) of the Yi water": Yi water being an old name for the Zi River.
candidates.fit: Holds the old Yiyang county seat and the prefecture city centre; region 14 holds the rest of the urban area.
candidates.recognisability: Current prefecture city (4.4M prefecture).
candidates.source_note: 益阳县 202 BC-1911, 益阳州 seat at 益阳市区 (CHGIS)

regions.notes: Yiyang (益阳) and Yueyang (岳阳) differ in characters but read alike on the map; same Hunan province, adjacent areas.

regions.summary: Lower Miluo and Xiangyin, with Changsha's northern edge (Kaifu, Wangcheng, Changsha county).

candidates.name: Xiangyin
candidates.meaning: "North (shaded side) of the Xiang": the county lies at the Xiang's mouth on Dongting Lake.
candidates.fit: Holds 47% of the county, which is 26% of the region; the biggest single unit after Miluo, whose name is taken.
candidates.recognisability: Current county; also seat of Xiangyin (474-1911) in CHGIS.
candidates.source_note: 湘阴县 474-1911 seat north of Xiangyin town

candidates.name: Luoxian
candidates.meaning: Qin county (222 BC to 624) that covered today's Miluo and parts of Pingjiang and Xiangyin; Luo is the old kingdom Luozi.
candidates.fit: Seat lay inside Miluo's Qu Yuan farm area, in this region; territory covered Miluo, the region's largest unit.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 225 hits with 湖南, top ones about this place.
candidates.source_note: 秦置。辖境大约位于今湖南省汨罗市和平江县、湘阴县部分

regions.notes: This region holds Miluo's urban centre (692k) but region 7 has the Miluo label; the Changsha batch may name Kaifu/Wangcheng parts nearby.

regions.summary: Taojiang (35%), Ziyang and Heshan districts, and the old Yuanjiang town: Zi River lowlands.

candidates.name: Taojiang
candidates.meaning: "Peach blossom river": named for the Taohua River; the county was split off Yiyang in 1952.
candidates.fit: Holds 59% of the county, which is 35% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 以境内桃花江得名

candidates.name: Yuanjiang
candidates.meaning: Named for the Yuan River.
candidates.fit: Holds the old Yuanjiang county seat (598-1911) and city centre, but only 31% of the city and 16% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.
candidates.source_note: 沅江县 598-1911 seat at 沅江市城区

candidates.name: Ziyang
candidates.meaning: "North bank of the Zi": a Yiyang city district.
candidates.fit: Holds 67% of the district, 25% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Same characters as the much larger Ziyang in Sichuan.
candidates.source_note: 因辖境大部分位于资水以北得名“资阳”

regions.notes: Yuanjiang is also offered in region 6.

regions.summary: Anhua county (73%) and western Taojiang: the Zi River gorges in the Xuefeng foothills.

candidates.name: Anhua
candidates.meaning: "Peace and civilisation": the county was cut from Meishan land in 1073 after the Song conquest of the Meishan peoples.
candidates.fit: Holds 99% of the county, which is 73% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county, known for Anhua dark tea.
candidates.source_note: 梅山，在今湖南新化县和安化县境内山地

candidates.name: Meishan
candidates.meaning: Mountain district of the Meishan 'cave peoples', conquered by the Song in 977; Anhua is the core of Meishan culture.
candidates.fit: Spans this region and region 16 (Xinhua); no single seat.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 222 hits with 湖南 but several are Ningbo's Meishan island.
candidates.source_note: 梅山，在今湖南新化县和安化县境内山地

regions.notes: Meishan is also offered in region 16; use it in at most one.

regions.summary: Xinhua county (99%): upper Zi River valley in the Xuefeng mountains.

candidates.name: Xinhua
candidates.meaning: "New civilisation": county formed in 1072 from the conquered Meishan lands.
candidates.fit: Holds 83% of the county, which is 99% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 新化县 1072-1911, seat at Baixi

candidates.name: Meishan
candidates.meaning: Mountain district of the Meishan 'cave peoples', in Xinhua and Anhua counties.
candidates.fit: Xinhua is half of Meishan; spans this region and region 15.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 222 hits with 湖南, some about Ningbo.
candidates.source_note: 梅山，在今湖南新化县和安化县境内山地

regions.notes: Meishan is also offered in region 15.

regions.summary: Lianyuan (48%), Lengshuijiang (30%) and edges of Xinhua and Xinshao.

candidates.name: Lianyuan
candidates.meaning: "Source of the Lian": the Lian River rises here; it was Lantian county until 1952.
candidates.fit: Holds 62% of the city, 48% of the region; 1.16M city figure is the whole county-level city.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.
candidates.source_note: 以地处涟水源头而得名

candidates.name: Lengshuijiang
candidates.meaning: "Cold water river": from the cold well water along the stream.
candidates.fit: Holds 99.7% of the city, 30% of the region; its Xikuangshan is the world's antimony capital.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.
candidates.source_note: 因境内涟溪两岸多井，井水极冷而得名

regions.summary: Loudi urban area (Louxing, 37%), Shuangfeng county (40%) and part of Lianyuan.

candidates.name: Loudi
candidates.meaning: Probably 'under the little hill' (naodi), alternatively said to be where the Lou and Di stars shine together.
candidates.fit: Holds the whole of the prefecture seat Louxing.
candidates.recognisability: Current prefecture city (3.9M).
candidates.source_note: 娄底一名起源于“垴底”...因地处“娄星和氐星交相辉映之处”

candidates.name: Shuangfeng
candidates.meaning: "Twin peaks": named for the Shuangfeng mountain.
candidates.fit: Holds 99% of the county, 40% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 得名于县境内的双峰山
